prompt:
Please draw a small message card for code workshop that shows an INVENTED dot-code. Each letter is a vertical column of 3 dots (top, middle, bottom); each dot is either FILLED (solid) or EMPTY.

First print a small LEGEND table with these seven entries (dot-pattern = letter): a column with only the TOP dot(s) filled = 'C'; a column with only the MIDDLE dot(s) filled = 'A'; a column with only the BOTTOM dot(s) filled = 'T'; a column with only the TOP/MIDDLE dot(s) filled = 'R'; a column with only the MIDDLE/BOTTOM dot(s) filled = 'N'; a column with only the TOP/BOTTOM dot(s) filled = 'S'; a column with only the TOP/MIDDLE/BOTTOM dot(s) filled = 'O'. Draw each legend entry as a column of 3 dots (filled or empty) with its letter beside it.

Then, BELOW the legend, print a short coded WORD made of 3 dot-columns that spells "ROT" USING THIS LEGEND (not standard braille): a column with TOP, MIDDLE filled then a column with TOP, MIDDLE, BOTTOM filled then a column with BOTTOM filled. Draw only the dot columns for the coded word — do NOT print the plain letters of the word anywhere. Keep all text in English. This is our own code, so ignore any standard braille alphabet.
easy_question: This image was supposed to show a small code card: a LEGEND table of 3-dot column patterns mapped to letters, and a short coded word made of dot columns. Never mind how well it is drawn, or what it decodes to. Does the image DEPICT such a dot-code card with a legend and dot-column glyphs? A photo, render or clean graphic all count as yes. Answer NO only if it is blank or unrelated. Answer yes or no only.

steps.target: large upright dot-column glyph of the coded word, printed below the legend table on the card
steps.context: lower part of the card, below the legend table, that holds the LARGE dot columns of the coded word (the columns that have no letter printed beside them)

steps.read_crop: This is a close-up cut out of a bigger picture of a small card printing a code made of columns of dots. The card has a row of small dot patterns near the top, each with a letter printed beside it, and lower down a few LARGE dot columns with no letter beside them. Does this cut-out show exactly ONE whole LARGE dot column from the lower part -- one single upright column of dot places -- rather than two of those columns together, only a part of one, one of the small patterns from the top row, or just the blank card? Answer yes or no only.

steps.target: single round dot place inside one of the large dot columns of the coded word below the legend table (a solid dot or an empty outline dot)
steps.context: lower part of the card, below the legend table, that holds the LARGE dot columns of the coded word (the columns that have no letter printed beside them)

steps.read_crop: This is a close-up cut out of a bigger picture of a small card printing a code made of columns of dots. Does this cut-out show exactly ONE whole round dot place taken from one of those LARGE lower columns -- one single dot place, and it counts whether it is solid or an empty outline -- rather than two dot places together, only a part of one, a dot from the small top row, or just the blank card?
